title: Kingdom of Soissons
capsule: The Kingdom of Soissons was a rump Roman domain in northwestern Gaul ruled by Syagrius, son of the Gallo-Roman general Aegidius, surviving for roughly a decade after the formal end of the Western Roman Empire in 476. Gregory of Tours styled Syagrius rex Romanorum, though scholars debate whether his authority constituted a kingdom or merely a military command; his territory encompassed the civitates around Soissons and extended into the Seine basin. In 486 the Frankish king Clovis I defeated Syagrius at the Battle of Soissons with an army the sources place in the tens of thousands, forcing him to flee to the Visigothic court of Alaric II; returned at Clovis's demand, Syagrius was executed, and his territory absorbed into the Frankish realm.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political entity is attested primarily through Gregory of Tours writing a century later; territorial extent is inferred from civitas boundaries and is contested in modern scholarship, with some historians reducing it to a single city-region.
